python.name: Python
python.about: Python from zero: basics (weeks 1-5), automation for Linux admin work (weeks 6-9), first machine learning (weeks 10-12).

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 1: Python Basics

lessons.title: Your first program
steps: Start menu → type `IDLE` → open it (it came with Python)
Type `print("Hello Hemanth")` and press Enter
File → New File, write 3 `print()` lines, save as `C:\CloudLab\python\hello.py`, press F5 to run

lessons.title: Variables and input
steps: `name = input("Your name: ")` then `print("Hi", name)`
`age = int(input("Age: "))` then `print(age + 1)` (int() turns text into a number)
Save as `about_me.py` and run it with F5

lessons.title: Numbers and text
steps: Try `+ - * /`, then `7 // 2` and `7 % 2` (whole part and remainder)
Text tricks: `"hemanth".upper()`, `len("server1")`, `" hi ".strip()`
Mini task: `tip.py` asks the bill amount and prints a 10% tip

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 2: if-else and Flow Control

lessons.title: if / elif / else
steps: `marks = int(input("Marks: "))`
`if marks >= 90:` print A, `elif marks >= 60:` print B, `else:` print C (4 spaces before each print)
Save as `grade.py` and test with 95, 70 and 30

lessons.title: for loops
steps: `for i in range(1, 11):` then `print(5, "x", i, "=", 5 * i)`
Change 5 to `int(input("Number: "))` so it prints any table
Loop over text: `for ch in "linux":` then `print(ch)`

lessons.title: while loop game
steps: `import random` and `secret = random.randint(1, 20)`
`while True:` ask a guess, print higher or lower, `break` when it's right
Save as `guess.py` and play it once

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 6: Lists
Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 7: Dictionaries

lessons.title: Lists
steps: `tasks = ["linux", "python", "c"]` then `print(tasks[0])`
Try `tasks.append("gym")`, `tasks.remove("c")`, `tasks.sort()`, `len(tasks)`
Print each one with `for t in tasks:`

lessons.title: Dictionaries
steps: `ports = {"ssh": 22, "http": 80, "https": 443}`
`print(ports["ssh"])`, add `ports["dns"] = 53`, try `ports.get("ftp", "unknown")`
Print all with `for name, num in ports.items():`

lessons.title: Mini project: marks report
steps: Make a dict of 4 subjects and marks
Print each subject, the total, and the average (`sum(marks.values()) / len(marks)`)
Print the best subject with `max(marks, key=marks.get)`

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 4: Functions

lessons.title: Functions
steps: `def square(n):` and inside it `return n * n`
Call it: `print(square(4))`
Write `greet(name)` that returns "Hello " + name (write once, use many times)

lessons.title: Modules and pip
steps: `import math` → `math.sqrt(16)`; `import datetime` → `datetime.date.today()`
PowerShell: `python -m pip install requests` (installs a module)
Check: `python -c "import requests; print(requests.__version__)"`

lessons.title: Mini project: unit converter
steps: Write `km_to_miles(km)` and `c_to_f(c)`
A small menu: `input()` asks 1 or 2 and calls the right function
Save as `convert.py`

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 10: Reading and Writing Files
Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 5: Debugging

lessons.title: Write and read files
steps: `with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:` then `f.write("hello\n")`
Read it back: `with open("notes.txt") as f:` then `print(f.read())`
Use `"a"` instead of `"w"` to add lines without deleting

lessons.title: Errors (don't panic)
steps: Make errors on purpose: `print(x)` → NameError, `int("abc")` → ValueError
Read the LAST line of the red text first; it names the problem
Catch one: `try:` `n = int(input())` `except ValueError:` `print("numbers only")`

lessons.title: Mini project: daily learn log
steps: Ask for one line: what did you learn today?
Add it to `learned.txt` with the date (`datetime.date.today()`)
Menu option 2 prints everything saved

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 11: Organizing Files

lessons.title: Look at folders with Python
steps: `from pathlib import Path` and `folder = Path("C:/CloudLab")`
`for p in folder.iterdir():` then `print(p.name)`
Find all .py files: `for p in folder.glob("**/*.py"): print(p)`

lessons.title: Auto-sort a folder
steps: Make a TEST folder `C:\CloudLab\sortme` with a few copied .txt, .jpg, .pdf files
Script: for each file, make a folder named after its extension and `shutil.move()` it there
Run it only on the test folder

lessons.title: Python on your Linux server
steps: In the Rocky VM: `python3 --version`
`vi hello.py` → `print("hi from server1")` → `python3 hello.py`
Add `#!/usr/bin/env python3` as line 1, then `chmod +x hello.py` and `./hello.py`

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 9: Regular Expressions
Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 18: CSV, JSON and XML

lessons.title: Read a log file
steps: VM: `sudo cp /var/log/messages ~/messages.txt` and `sudo chown hemanth ~/messages.txt`
Script: count all lines, and lines containing "error" (use `.lower()`)
Print the last 5 error lines

lessons.title: Regex: find patterns
steps: `import re` then `re.findall(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+", text)` finds IP addresses
Save `ip a` output to a file (`ip a > ip.txt`) and run it on that
Ask Vega to explain the pattern piece by piece

lessons.title: Save a report as CSV
steps: `import csv` and write rows like `["line", "message"]` to `errors.csv`
Look at it with `cat errors.csv`
Read it back with `csv.reader`

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 12: Command Line Programs

lessons.title: Run Linux commands from Python
steps: `import subprocess`
`r = subprocess.run(["df", "-h"], capture_output=True, text=True)` then `print(r.stdout)`
Try `["uptime"]` and `["free", "-m"]`

lessons.title: Server health check
steps: VM: `pip3 install --user psutil`
Print `psutil.cpu_percent(1)`, `psutil.virtual_memory().percent`, `psutil.disk_usage("/").percent`
If disk is above 80, print WARNING (this is your resume project, Server Health Monitor)

lessons.title: Make it a real tool
steps: `import logging` and write results to `health.log` instead of printing
`import argparse` so `./health.py --disk 85` sets the limit
Run it 3 times, then `cat health.log`

learn: Automate the Boring Stuff, ch 19: Scheduling Tasks

lessons.title: Talk to a web API
steps: `import requests` then `r = requests.get("https://api.github.com/users/torvalds")`
`data = r.json()` then print `data["name"]` and `data["public_repos"]`
Try it with your own GitHub username

lessons.title: Settings in a YAML file
steps: VM: `pip3 install --user pyyaml`
Make `limits.yaml` with `disk: 85` and `memory: 80` on two lines
Load it in health.py with `yaml.safe_load()` and use those numbers

lessons.title: Run it every 5 minutes (cron)
steps: `crontab -e` and add `*/5 * * * * /home/hemanth/health.py >> /home/hemanth/cron.log 2>&1`
Wait 10 minutes, then `cat ~/health.log`
Push health.py to your GitHub repo

lessons.title: NumPy basics
steps: PowerShell: `python -m pip install numpy pandas matplotlib`
`import numpy as np` then `a = np.array([10, 20, 30])`; try `a * 2`, `a.mean()`, `a.max()`
Why: ML libraries use these arrays underneath

lessons.title: pandas: tables in Python
steps: Make `marks.csv` with columns name,subject,marks (5 rows)
`import pandas as pd`, `df = pd.read_csv("marks.csv")`, then `df.head()` and `df.describe()`
Filter: `df[df["marks"] > 60]`; average per subject: `df.groupby("subject")["marks"].mean()`

lessons.title: Charts
steps: `import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`
`df.groupby("subject")["marks"].mean().plot(kind="bar")` then `plt.show()`
Save it: `plt.savefig("marks.png")`

lessons.title: What is machine learning
steps: ML = the computer learns a pattern from examples, instead of you writing the rules
Words: features (inputs), label (the answer), training, testing
Do Kaggle Intro to ML, lesson 1 (How Models Work)

lessons.title: Your first model
steps: `python -m pip install scikit-learn`
`from sklearn.datasets import load_iris` then `X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)`
`model = DecisionTreeClassifier().fit(X, y)` then compare `model.predict(X[:5])` with `y[:5]`

lessons.title: Test it fairly
steps: `train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)` hides 20% of the data for testing
Train on the train part, check `accuracy_score` on the test part
Why: testing on data it already saw is cheating (overfitting)

lessons.title: Compare two models
steps: Use `load_wine` data this time
Try `DecisionTreeClassifier` and `KNeighborsClassifier`; print both accuracies
Write in your notes which one won

lessons.title: Save and share
steps: `import joblib`; `joblib.dump(model, "model.pkl")`, then load it back and predict
Push the project with a short README to GitHub

lessons.title: Review: what you can do now
steps: Press Quiz me in Ask Vega
List 3 scripts you made that you can explain in an interview
Plan what's next with Vega (more automation, more ML)

c.name: C
c.about: C from zero on your Linux server (gcc + vi): basics, pointers and memory, then simple data structures.

learn: learn-c.org: Hello, World! (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: Install gcc and say hello
steps: VM: `sudo dnf install -y gcc`
`vi hello.c` and type: `#include <stdio.h>` / `int main(void) {` / `printf("Hello\n");` / `return 0; }`
`gcc hello.c -o hello` then `./hello`

lessons.title: Variables and printf
steps: `int age = 21; float cgpa = 8.5; char grade = 'A';`
`printf("%d %.1f %c\n", age, cgpa, grade);`
Remember: %d whole number, %f decimal, %c letter, %s text

learn: learn-c.org: Variables and Types (try it in the browser)
learn-c.org: Conditions (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: scanf and maths
steps: `int a, b; scanf("%d %d", &a, &b);` (& means: store it here)
Print the sum, difference and product
Try `a / b` (whole numbers only!) and `a % b` (remainder)

lessons.title: if / else and switch
steps: Even or odd: `if (n % 2 == 0)`
A menu with `switch (choice) { case 1: ... break; }`

learn: learn-c.org: For loops (try it in the browser)
learn-c.org: While loops (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: for and while
steps: Table of 7: `for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++)`
Count down from 10 to 1 with `while`

lessons.title: Loop practice
steps: Sum of the digits of a number (use `% 10` and `/ 10`)
Print a triangle of stars with two loops

learn: learn-c.org: Functions (try it in the browser)
learn-c.org: Recursion (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: Functions
steps: `int square(int n) { return n * n; }` above main, then call it in main
Write `max(a, b)` yourself

lessons.title: Recursion
steps: A function that calls itself: `factorial(n)`
Return 1 if n <= 1, else `n * factorial(n - 1)`; try n = 5 (answer 120)

learn: learn-c.org: Arrays (try it in the browser)
learn-c.org: Strings (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: Arrays
steps: Loop to find the total, average and highest mark

lessons.title: Strings
steps: `char name[20] = "hemanth";` and `printf("%s\n", name);`
`#include <string.h>` → `strlen(name)`; print the name backwards with a loop

learn: learn-c.org: Pointers (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: What a pointer is
steps: A pointer stores an address: where a value lives in memory
`int x = 10; int *p = &x;` then print `x`, `*p`, and `p` (with `%p`)

lessons.title: Pointers in practice
steps: Write `swap(int *a, int *b)` and call `swap(&x, &y)`
Why: without pointers the function only changes copies

learn: learn-c.org: Structures (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: struct
steps: `struct student { char name[20]; int marks; };`
Make one student, fill it in, print it

lessons.title: Array of structs
steps: 3 students: `struct student s[3];`
Print who has the highest marks

learn: learn-c.org: Dynamic allocation (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: malloc and free
steps: `#include <stdlib.h>` then `int *nums = malloc(5 * sizeof(int));`
Fill and print it, then `free(nums);`

lessons.title: Finding bugs
steps: Compile with warnings: `gcc -Wall -g file.c -o file`
Read the FIRST error line; send Vega a photo if stuck
Segmentation fault = using memory you don't own (usually a bad pointer or array index)

learn: CS50x week 4: Memory (file I/O part) (video + notes)

lessons.title: Write and read files
steps: `FILE *f = fopen("notes.txt", "w"); fprintf(f, "hello\n"); fclose(f);`
Read it back with `fgets()` in a loop

lessons.title: Mini project: marks saver
steps: Ask for 3 names and marks, save them to `marks.txt`
A second run reads and prints them

lessons.title: Search
steps: Linear search: check each item one by one
Binary search on a sorted array: cut it in half each time

lessons.title: Bubble sort
steps: Two loops: swap neighbours that are in the wrong order
Print the array after each pass to watch it sort

learn: learn-c.org: Linked lists (try it in the browser)

lessons.title: Build a linked list
steps: `struct node { int value; struct node *next; };`
Make 3 nodes with malloc, link them, print them by following `next`

lessons.title: Add and remove
steps: Insert a node at the start; delete a value
Free all nodes at the end

lessons.title: Stack and queue
steps: Stack with an array: push and pop (last in, first out)
Queue: first in, first out

lessons.title: Review
steps: Press Quiz me in Ask Vega
Put your C files in your GitHub repo
